inputs.text: [happily] Listen to what comes next: the very first oceans have just been born. [curious] And guess what shows up in them...
[chuckles][playful] Not yet! Long before fish, [softly] tiny living things, too small to see: bacteria. [calm] The very first living things on Earth.
[softly] So tiny that thousands could fit on the tip of a pencil. [pauses] And some of them are special: the cyanobacteria.
[excited][calm] They breathe in sunlight! [gasps] They turn it into food, and while they make their food, they let out something precious: oxygen, the air we breathe.
[amazed] For hundreds of millions of years, they make so much of it that the air on Earth changes completely. [serious] Scientists call this the Great Oxidation.
[gasps] The air we breathe today… does it come from those tiny bacteria?
[happily] A good part of it, yes! [chuckles] And meanwhile, in the ocean, life keeps coming up with new things.
[excited][quickly] Algae, [gasps] soft little animals, [calm] and then the very first animals with shells.
[amazed] Does all that take a long time?
[calm][softly] Hundreds of millions of years. [pauses] Life is never in a hurry. [warmly] But it never stops inventing.
